title.zh: 卷三十四 蜀書四 二主妃子傳
title.en: Volume 34: Book of Shu 4 - Biographies of concubines and sons of the two Lords
title.raw: 卷三十四 蜀書四 二主妃子傳 Volume 34: Book of Shu 4 - Biographies of concubines and sons of the two Lords

sentences.zh: 先主甘皇后

translations.literal: Empress Gan of the First Lord
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gan, consort of Liu Bei (styled the First Lord)

sentences.zh: 先主甘皇后，沛人也。

translations.literal: Empress Gan of the First Lord was a native of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gan came from Pei.

sentences.zh: 先主臨豫州，住小沛，納以為妾。

translations.literal: When the First Lord came to Yu prefecture and dwelt at Little Pei, he took her in as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei held Yuzhou and made his base at Xiaopei, he took her as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 先主數喪嫡室，常攝內事。

translations.literal: The First Lord repeatedly lost his principal wives, and she constantly managed affairs within the household.
translations.idiomatic: He had buried several chief wives in succession, so she habitually ran the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 隨先主於荊州，產後主。

translations.literal: She followed the First Lord in Jing province and bore the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhou she gave birth to the future emperor Liu Shan.

sentences.zh: 值曹公軍至，追及先主於當陽長阪，於時困偪，棄後及後主，賴趙雲保護，得免於難。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao’s army arrived and overtook the First Lord at Changban Slope in Dangyang, at that time hard pressed, he abandoned the empress and the Later Lord; thanks to Zhao Yun’s protection they escaped the peril.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao’s host caught Liu Bei at Changban in Dangyang, the retreat was so desperate that he abandoned Lady Gan and the boy; only Zhao Yun’s shielding brought them through alive.

sentences.zh: 後卒，葬於南郡。

translations.literal: Later she died and was buried in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: She died later and was interred in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 章武二年，追諡皇思夫人，遷葬於蜀，未至而先主殂隕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu she was posthumously titled Lady of Imperial Remembrance, and her burial was to be moved to Shu, but before it arrived the First Lord passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangwu 2 she received the posthumous title Lady of Imperial Remembrance and her coffin was ordered west into Shu, but Liu Bei died before the cortège arrived.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮上言：

translations.literal: The Chancellor Liang submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang memorialized as follows:

sentences.zh: 皇思夫人履行脩仁，淑慎其身。

translations.literal: The Lady of Imperial Remembrance practiced conduct and cultivated benevolence, chaste and careful in her person.
translations.idiomatic: The late Lady of Imperial Remembrance lived with integrity and kindness, modest and guarded in deportment.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝昔在上將，嬪妃作合，載育聖躬，大命不融。

translations.literal: The late emperor, in former days as a general, was matched with a consort who bore and nurtured his sacred person, yet the great mandate did not endure.
translations.idiomatic: When our late sovereign was still a field commander, she joined him in wedlock and bore his heir, though heaven cut that union short.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝存時，篤義垂恩，念皇思夫人神柩在遠飄颻，特遣使者奉迎。

translations.literal: While the late emperor lived he was deeply dutiful and showed favor, remembering that the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin drifted far away, and specially dispatched envoys to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: In his lifetime he never forgot her: learning her coffin still wandered far from the capital, he sent envoys to escort it home.

sentences.zh: 會大行皇帝崩，今皇思夫人神柩以到，又梓宮在道，園陵將成，安厝有期。

translations.literal: It happened that the late emperor died; now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin has arrived, and moreover the catalpa coffin is on the road, the mausoleum park nearly complete, and the date for laying her to rest is set.
translations.idiomatic: He has since died, yet her catafalque has now reached us while his own bier is still en route and the imperial tombs near completion, so both burials may soon be ordered.

sentences.zh: 臣輒與太常臣賴恭等議：《禮記》曰：『立愛自親始，教民孝也；

translations.literal: Your servant has rashly deliberated with Minister of Ceremonies Lai Gong and others: the Record of Rites says, ‘Establish love beginning with kin—this teaches the people filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: I have consulted Minister Lai Gong and others. The Book of Rites teaches, ‘Teach love by starting with one’s parents—thus the people learn filial piety;

sentences.zh: 立敬自長始，教民順也。

translations.literal: establish reverence beginning with elders—this teaches the people obedience.’
translations.idiomatic: teach respect by starting with one’s elders—thus the people learn deference.’

sentences.zh: 』不忘其親，所由生也。

translations.literal: ’ Not forgetting one’s kin is the source from which life proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: ’ To forget not those who gave you life is the root of all moral feeling.

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，母以子貴。

translations.literal: By the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the mother is honored because of her son.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn canon holds that a mother’s rank rises with her son’s.

sentences.zh: 昔高皇帝追尊太上昭靈夫人為昭靈皇后，孝和皇帝改葬其母梁貴人，尊號曰恭懷皇后，孝愍皇帝亦改葬其母王夫人，尊號曰靈懷皇后。

translations.literal: In antiquity the High Emperor posthumously honored the Grand Supreme Lady Zhao Ling as Empress Zhao Ling; Emperor Xiaohe reburied his mother the Honored Lady Liang with the title Empress Gonghuai; Emperor Xiaomin likewise reburied his mother Lady Wang with the title Empress Linghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han raised his mother to Empress Zhaoling; He-di reinterred Lady Liang as Empress Gonghuai; Min-di did the same for Lady Wang as Empress Linghuai.

sentences.zh: 今皇思夫人宜有尊號，以慰寒泉之思，輒與恭等案諡法，宜曰昭烈皇后。

translations.literal: Now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance ought to receive an exalted title to console thoughts from the cold spring; your servant has rashly with Gong and others examined the posthumous-title code—she should be called Empress Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: She therefore deserves a throne name that may comfort the living. We have weighed the statutes of posthumous honor and propose Empress Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 詩曰：『谷則異室，死則同穴。』

translations.literal: The Odes say, ‘In life we dwelt in different chambers; in death we share one grave.’
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, ‘We dwelt apart in life; we lie together in death.’

sentences.zh: 〈《禮》云：上古無合葬，中古後因時方有。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Rites states: In high antiquity there was no joint burial; from middle antiquity onward it arose with the times.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Rites note that joint burial was unknown in earliest ages and became practice only in later ages.〉

sentences.zh: 故昭烈皇后宜與大行皇帝合葬，臣請太尉告宗廟，布露天下，具禮儀別奏。

translations.literal: Therefore Empress Zhaolie ought to be buried with the late emperor; your servant requests the Grand Commandant announce this in the ancestral temples, publish it throughout the realm, and separately memorialize the full ritual observances.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask that she be laid beside the late emperor, that the grand commandant report this to the shrines of state, that an edict proclaim it to the realm, and that the detailed rites be submitted in a further memorial.

sentences.zh: 制曰可。

translations.literal: The rescript said: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign’s reply read: Granted.

sentences.zh: 先主穆皇后

translations.literal: Empress Mu of the First Lord
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mu, empress of Liu Bei

sentences.zh: 後主敬哀皇后

translations.literal: Empress Jing’ai of the Later Lord
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jing’ai of Liu Shan

sentences.zh: 後主敬哀皇后，車騎將軍張飛長女也。

translations.literal: Empress Jing’ai of the Later Lord was the eldest daughter of General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan’s Empress Jing’ai was the eldest daughter of Zhang Fei, general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 章武元年，納為太子妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhangwu she was taken in as heir’s consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangwu 1 she entered the palace as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxing 1 saw her enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨，葬南陵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year she died and was buried at Nan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifteenth Jianxing year and was buried at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 後主張皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhang of the Later Lord
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang of Liu Shan’s reign

sentences.zh: 先主子 永

translations.literal: The First Lord’s son Yong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong, son of Liu Bei

sentences.zh: 先主子 理

translations.literal: The First Lord’s son Li
translations.idiomatic: Liu Li, son of Liu Bei

sentences.zh: 劉理字奉孝，亦後主庶弟也，與永異母。

translations.literal: Liu Li, courtesy Fengxiao, was also a younger half-brother of the Later Lord by a different mother from Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Li, styled Fengxiao, was another younger half-brother of Liu Shan, not born to the same mother as Liu Yong.

sentences.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立理為梁王，策曰：「小子理，朕統承漢序，祗順天命，遵脩典秩，建爾於東，為漢籓輔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Li as Prince of Liang; the patent read, "Young Li, We inherit the sequence of Han, reverently obey Heaven’s mandate, observe canonical order, and establish you in the east as a feudal bulwark of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Li as prince of Liang. The edict ran: “Young Liu Li, I carry on Han’s line, bow to heaven’s charge, and uphold the statutes; I therefore enfeoff you in the east as a feudal shield of the house of Han.

sentences.zh: 惟彼梁土，畿甸之邦，民狎教化，易導以禮。

translations.literal: That land of Liang is a domain within the capital region; the people are intimate with instruction and easily guided by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Liang lies within the royal domain; its people are used to civilizing rule and readily led by ritual.

sentences.zh: 往悉乃心，懷保黎庶，以永爾國，王其敬之哉！

translations.literal: Go forth with all your heart, cherish and protect the black-haired masses, and thereby perpetuate your state—may you, my prince, revere these words!
translations.idiomatic: Go with a whole heart, shelter the common folk, and so long preserve your state—revere this charge, my prince!

sentences.zh: 」建興八年，改封理為安平王。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year of Jianxing Li’s fief was changed to Prince of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Jianxing 8 his title was changed to prince of Anping.

sentences.zh: 延熙七年卒，諡曰悼王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanxi he died; his posthumous title was Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanxi 7 and received the posthumous epithet Prince Dao (Lamented).

sentences.zh: 子哀王胤嗣，十九年卒。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ai Yin succeeded; in the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin, prince Ai, succeeded and died in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子殤王承嗣，二十年卒。

translations.literal: His son Prince Shang Cheng succeeded; in the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, prince Shang, followed and died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 景耀四年詔曰：「安平王，先帝所命。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyao an edict said, "The Prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyao 4 brought an edict: “The prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late sovereign.

sentences.zh: 三世早夭，國嗣頹絕，朕用傷悼。

translations.literal: Three generations have died young in succession, and the line of succession has broken off; We are thereby grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Three heirs in a row have perished young, leaving the fief without an heir, and We mourn that break.

sentences.zh: 其以武邑侯輯襲王位。

translations.literal: Let Marquis of Wuyi Ji succeed to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore order Ji, marquis of Wuyi, to inherit the princedom.

sentences.zh: 」輯，理子也，咸熙元年，東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封鄉侯。

translations.literal: " Ji was Li’s son; in the first year of Xianxi he moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ji was Liu Li’s son. In Xianxi 1 he went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 後主太子 璿

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of the Later Lord
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, crown prince of Liu Shan

sentences.zh: 後主太子璿，字文衡。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of the Later Lord, courtesy Wenheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, styled Wenheng, was Liu Shan’s heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 母王貴人，本敬哀張皇后侍人也。

translations.literal: His mother was Honored Lady Wang, originally a handmaid of Empress Jing’ai née Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Wang, once a maid to Empress Jing’ai of the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年正月策曰：「在昔帝王，繼體立嗣，副貳國統，古今常道。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yanxi the patent said, "Of old emperors and kings, continuing the body and establishing the heir, appointing a deputy for the state’s succession, has been the constant way from ancient to present.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 1 opened with an edict: “Since antiquity sovereigns have named heirs to carry on the flesh and serve as second to the throne—

sentences.zh: 今以璿為皇太子，昭顯祖宗之威，命使行丞相事左將軍朗持節授印緩。

translations.literal: Now We make Xuan crown prince, to manifest the majesty of the ancestors; We order Lang, acting as chancellor and general of the left, to bear the tally and confer seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore invest Liu Xuan as crown prince so the ancestors’ awe may shine abroad, and We dispatch Lang, left general acting as chancellor, with the imperial baton to present his seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 其勉脩茂質，祗恪道義，諮詢典禮，敬友師傅，斟酌眾善，翼成爾德，可不務脩以自勗哉！

translations.literal: Strive to cultivate a rich nature, reverently keep to the Way and its duties, consult the canons of ritual, respectfully befriend your tutors, weigh the counsel of many good men, and thereby wing your virtue—can you fail to labor at cultivation and urge yourself onward!
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate excellence in yourself, hold fast to duty and the moral law, study the rites, honor your teachers, sift good counsel from many voices, and so grow into virtue—how could you not strive to improve and press yourself forward?

sentences.zh: 」時年十五。

translations.literal: " At that time he was fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was fifteen sui at the time.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年冬，蜀亡。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Jingyao Shu fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jingyao 6 the state of Shu was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 咸熙元年正月，鍾會作亂於成都，璿為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xianxi Zhong Hui raised rebellion in Chengdu, and Xuan was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xianxi 1 Zhong Hui mutinied at Chengdu, and Liu Xuan was cut down by the riotous soldiery.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：璿弟，瑤、琮、瓚、諶、恂、璩六人。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng’s Genealogy of Shu states: Xuan had younger brothers Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu—six men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng’s Shu genealogy lists six younger brothers: Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu.

sentences.zh: 蜀敗，諶自殺，餘皆內徙。

translations.literal: When Shu fell, Chen committed suicide; the rest were moved inward.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu collapsed Chen took his own life; the others were deported to the interior.

sentences.zh: 值永嘉大亂，子孫絕滅。

translations.literal: They encountered the great turmoil of Yongjia, and descendants were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongjia upheavals wiped out their posterity.

sentences.zh: 唯永孫玄奔蜀，李雄偽署安樂公以嗣禪後。

translations.literal: Only Yong’s grandson Xuan fled to Shu, and Li Xiong falsely installed him as duke of Anle to continue the line after Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Yong’s grandson Liu Xuan escaped back into Shu, where Li Xiong named him duke of Anle in mock succession to Liu Shan.

sentences.zh: 永和三年討李勢，盛參戎行，見玄於成都也。〉

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, when Li Shi was campaigned against, Sheng took part in the army and saw Xuan at Chengdu.〉
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 3, during the expedition against Li Shi, Sun Sheng himself saw Liu Xuan in Chengdu.〉

translations.literal: 【Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 評曰：易稱有夫婦然後有父子，夫人倫之始，恩紀之隆，莫尚於此矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The Changes says that husband and wife come first, then father and son; nowhere in the beginnings of human relations or the depth of affection and duty is anything higher than this.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Book of Changes places husband and wife before father and son; no bond in the human order runs deeper or begins earlier.

sentences.zh: 是故紀錄，以究一國之體焉。

translations.literal: Therefore they are recorded here, to exhaust the pattern of a single state.
translations.idiomatic: They are set down in this chapter so the reader may grasp how one kingdom ordered its inner house.
